rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes an aging heat treatment to induce B2 precipitates, while the target paper added 4.2 at.% Cr via arc melting to form a Laves phase. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (heat treatment vs. composition change).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature creep/tensile testing at 850–900°C, whereas the target paper performed room-temperature compression testing. These are completely different temperature and loading regimes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes precipitation strengthening from nanoscale B2 precipitates, while the target paper describes a dual mechanism of solid solution hardening and crack hindrance from a reticulated Laves phase. These are different mechanism classes with different structural mediators.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts enhanced high-temperature strength and creep resistance with unchanged room-temperature properties, while the target paper reports a concurrent increase in room-temperature yield strength and fracture strain. The predicted property direction and conditions differ.
